aceStatus.description:
CdoId: 1110; FieldId: 673187861; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure)
Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully
3	ACEFFail	                an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event
> 99	<custom status>	User specific status codes (Designer based)

verifyComputerName.description:
CdoId: 1110; FieldId: 689965530; Workspace: 60; Flags: None; Annotations: Flag indicating whether the computer name is to be verified. Verification will be done if all of the following are met:
i)	Computer Name is passed in.
ii)	Computer Group is assigned to the Verify Container's Spec.
iii)	The Verify Computer Name service flag is set to true.

specification.description:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20172; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: String representation of the current Spec. An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.

A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.

See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

status.description:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20174; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. 
Valid values and their meanings are:
0 = Deleted
1 = Active
2 = Closed
3 = In Transit (shipped)
4 = Issued (component)
A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

verifyComputerName.description:
CdoId: 2180; FieldId: 689965566; Workspace: 60; Flags: None; Annotations: Flag indicating whether the computer name is to be verified. Verification will be done if all of the following are met:

ii)	Computer Name not found in the group.

CdoId: 2180; FieldId: 689965571; Workspace: 60; Flags: None; Annotations: Event used to indicate when to calculate yield. Expected values include:

CdoId: 1110; FieldId: 673187861; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure)
Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully
3	ACEFFail	                an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event
> 99	<custom status>	User specific status codes (Designer based)

0 = Deleted
1 = Active
2 = Closed
3 = In Transit (shipped)
4 = Issued (component)
A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully

displayName.description: CdoId: 3590; FieldId: 26059; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. clearLocation.description:
CdoId: 2650; FieldId: 2028; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: This field is used to clear the Location field associated to the container being moved in.  

Locations define physical areas within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. 

In some cases, such as when storage racks are used to hold containers before a particular operation, the Location (ie, Rack ID) needs to be cleared when the container is move into the operation (and onto processing equipment).

overrideCurrentStatus.description: CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 2852; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The intent of this field is to enable the client application to override the current status of the container (the step where the container is located at the beginning of the transaction). This field should only be used for advanced automation systems where there is a virtual certainty that the automation system holds the correct information about the current location of the container.  This allows the automation system to perform moves easily after the InSite has been taken offline and brought back up for database maintenance, etc.  Note that there are no history records generated for the moves "missed".

overrideCurrentStatus.description: CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 2852; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The intent of this field is to enable the client application to override the current status of the container (the step where the container is located at the beginning of the transaction).  If the client application sets this field to "True"  the transaction will assume the container is at the operation/step the client specifies, instead of using the operation/step of the container.  This field should only be used for advanced automation systems where there is a virtual certainty that the automation system holds the correct information about the current location of the container.  This allows the automation system to perform moves easily after the InSite has been taken offline and brought back up for database maintenance, etc.  Note that there are no history records generated for the moves "missed".

verifyComputerName.description:
CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 689965603; Workspace: 60; Flags: None; Annotations: Flag indicating whether the computer name is to be verified. Verification will be done if all of the following are met:

i)	Computer Name is not configured as a Computer.
ii)	Computer Name not found in the group.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully

overrideCurrentStatus.description: CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 2852; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The intent of this field is to enable the client application to override the current status of the container (the step where the container is located at the beginning of the transaction).  If the client application sets this field to "True"  the transaction will assume the container is at the operation/step the client specifies, instead of using the operation/step of the container.  This field should only be used for advanced automation systems where there is a virtual certainty that the automation system holds the correct information about the current location of the container.  This allows the automation system to perform moves easily after the InSite has been taken offline and brought back up for database maintenance, etc.  Note that there are no history records generated for the moves "missed".

eS_AvailableResources.description:
CdoId: 4841615; FieldId: 689968212; Workspace: 60; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

CdoId: 1110; FieldId: 673187861; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ACEStatus field indicates the success or failure of the after commit events (AfterCommit and AfterCommitEventFailure)
Enumeration for the after commit event status codes.

Value	Name	                Meaning
1	ACESuccess	after commit event completed successfully
2	ACEFSuccess	an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and after commit event failure event completed successfully
3	ACEFFail	                an unhandled error in the after commit event was caught and another unhandled error was raised in the after commit event failure event
